item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"medium","summary":"B is preferable because it preserves the existing Add test while adding focused retry and multipart Upload coverage. The implementations are otherwise nearly identical and share the same contract deviations.","reasons":["B retains TestFilesService_Add, preserving its method, path, content-type, and decoding assertions; A replaces it with a retry test that no longer checks method or path, weakening existing coverage.","B separately tests replay of an open-file Add body and verifies Upload multipart field name, filename, content, and retry behavior on every attempt.","B adds useful API documentation to Add explaining buffering and the distinction from Upload.","Both reuse multipartbody.NewFile and buffer Add bodies into bytes.Reader, giving the retry transport a replayable body."],"risks_a":["Upload calls the new private add helper instead of routing through the public Add method, contrary to the frozen contract.","It removes the original Add test and loses some request-construction assertions.","It adds no visible tests for empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures."],"risks_b":["Upload also bypasses Add via the private add helper, violating the explicit single-path requirement.","It adds no visible tests for empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures.","Its Add retry test does not itself verify Content-Type, though the retained existing Add test covers that behavior."]}
